statement: A rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex consists of: (a) a bounded-below cochain complex $K_{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces with a finite increasing filtration $W$ by subcomplexes, finite on each cochain group; (b) a cochain complex $K_{\mathbb C}$ of $\mathbb C$-vector spaces with a finite increasing filtration $W$ by subcomplexes and a finite decreasing filtration $F$ by subcomplexes, again finite on each cochain group; (c) a filtered comparison morphism $K_{\mathbb Q}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C\to K_{\mathbb C}$ which is a quasi-isomorphism; subject to the axiom: for every integer $w$ the weight-graded complex $\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK$ has finite-dimensional cohomology, its induced differential is strict for the induced filtration $F$, and for every $r$ the induced filtration $F$ on $H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK_{\mathbb C})$, together with the induced rational comparison, is a pure Hodge structure of weight $r+w$. The weight filtration on $H^n(K)$ is the shifted filtration $W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K)\bigr)$; this shift is essential and pole-count weight on a logarithmic complex is not the weight on its cohomology. The same definitions apply to bounded-below complexes of sheaves on a space when the complexes are replaced by derived global sections and the required resolutions preserve the graded pieces; the existence of such resolutions for the concrete complexes used later is proved where those complexes are constructed, not here.
strategy: Definition only, so no proof section. The axiom is a condition on the data (Deligne III (8.1.5) together with (8.1.1)-(8.1.2)); the displayed shift is the convention of (1.1.2), and it is what makes the axiom's weight $r+w$ compatible with the weight of $H^n$; the statement records this rather than proving it. The strictness requirement on the differentials of the graded complexes is exactly axiom (GH1); the standard equivalent formulation, that the $F$-spectral sequence of the graded complex degenerates at its first page, is recorded in the sources but is neither asserted nor used here, so no degeneration theorem enters the dependencies. Biregularity (finiteness on each cochain group) is what the filtered-complex comparison needs in the following lemma; it holds for the complexes occurring in this run. The sheaf clause is applied by resolving the graded pieces separately; a Godement resolution of a complex of sheaves has exact terms and successive cokernels, so it preserves the graded pieces, but the proof of that statement belongs to the pages that construct the sheaves. Choice-free at this level: no family of nonempty sets is selected.

statement: Let $S$ be a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety. A geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation on $S$ consists of a finite-rank rational local system $H$ ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]), a continuous pure Hodge decomposition of its fibers, or a finite direct sum of pure weights, in the sense of [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]], and an algebraic realization on a nonempty Zariski open $U\subseteq S$: there are smooth projective morphisms $f_i:X_i\to U$, degrees $m_i$ and integers $r_i$ such that $H|_U$ is a Hodge direct summand of $$\bigoplus_iR^{m_i}(f_i)_*\mathbb Q(r_i),$$ where $\mathbb Q(r)$ is the Tate structure of [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]. A Hodge direct summand means the image of a flat rational idempotent that is a Hodge morphism at every point. A morphism of variations is a flat rational map that is a Hodge morphism at every point. A polarization of a pure object is a flat rational bilinear form with the Hodge positivity property on every fiber; it is not postulated for arbitrary local subsystems: a geometric realization carries one by relative ampleness, and Hodge direct summands inherit it. The closures recorded here under finite sums, tensor products, Hodge direct summands and Tate twists, the exterior-power realizability, the duals via the polarization, and the full monodromy-stable integral lattices are proved by the family construction later on this page; that forward mention is explanatory and is not a prerequisite of the definition.
strategy: Definitional. Fixes the objects, morphisms, the direct-summand notion and the polarization convention consumed by the fixed-part and semisimplicity theorems of this page. Source route: the continuous-family and algebraic-family definitions and the closure verification of Deligne II 4.2.1-4.2.5 (continuous Q-Hodge families, polarizations, the conditions (4.2.2.1)-(4.2.2.4), the algebraic category of (4.2.4), and (4.2.5)(i)-(iii)). The only claim-like content is the closure/lattice contract, discharged on this page by the family lemma recorded in `justified_by`; nothing about arbitrary analytic variations is imported, and Schmid's unpublished footnote in Deligne II 4.2.6 is explicitly not used. No choice principle is needed: the definition quantifies over finite data.

statement: A rational mixed Hodge structure can be an extension of two pure structures and still admit no splitting over $\mathbb Q$. On $H=\mathbb Q e_0\oplus\mathbb Q e_1$ put $W_{-3}=0$, $W_{-2}=W_{-1}=\mathbb Q e_1$, $W_0=H$, and $F^1=0$, $F^0=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)$, $F^{-1}=H_{\mathbb C}$. This is a mixed Hodge structure sitting in a short exact sequence $0\to\mathbb Q(1)\to H\to\mathbb Q(0)\to0$ which has no splitting in the category of rational mixed Hodge structures.
strategy: Verification in two steps, both finite computations in the displayed basis. Step 1: compute the graded pieces. On $\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-2}=\mathbb Q e_1$ the filtration $F$ has $F^{-1}$ everything and $F^0=0$, so the Hodge type is $(-1,-1)$ and the piece is $\mathbb Q(1)$; on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_0=\mathbb Q e_0$ the image of $F^0$ in the quotient is everything and $F^1=0$, so the type is $(0,0)$ and the piece is $\mathbb Q(0)$. Both are $n$-opposed for their weights, so the axioms hold, and the degree-one map $\mathbb Q(1)\to H$ and the quotient map $H\to\mathbb Q(0)$ are morphisms of mixed Hodge structures with kernel and cokernel as displayed. Step 2: rule out rational splittings. A $\mathbb Q$-linear section of the quotient sends the rational generator of $\mathbb Q(0)$ to $e_0+\lambda e_1$ with $\lambda\in\mathbb Q$. A morphism of mixed Hodge structures must map $F^0\mathbb Q(0)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ into $F^0H_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)$, so $e_0+\lambda e_1\in\mathbb C(e_0+ie_1)$, forcing $\lambda=i$ by comparison of the $e_0$- and $e_1$-coefficients. No rational $\lambda$ does this, so no rational splitting exists. The verification uses only the definitions; it exhibits the non-split extension concretely and claims nothing about extensions of other weights or about integral structures.

statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). A rational projective curve $C$ with one ordinary node has one-dimensional $H^1(C,\mathbb Q)$ of weight $0$, illustrating that proper singular cohomology need not be pure of its degree.
strategy: Assume AC as inherited from [[thm-proper-cohomology-has-functorial-mixed-hodge-weights-at-most-degree]]. Source: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge III, (8.2.4)(iii) and (8.2.1)-(8.2.2) (weights at most degree on proper cohomology and its hypercover construction; printed pp. 38-39), read in full, together with the explicit normalization Cech computation below. [F1] The normalization $\nu:\mathbb P^1\to C$ identifies two distinct points $a,b$ to the node; $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)\cong S^2$ by [[thm-stereographic-projection-riemann-sphere-homeomorphism]], so $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ and $H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathbb Q)=0$ by [[cor-homology-of-spheres]] and [[cor-cohomology-over-a-field-is-dual-to-homology-over-that-field]]. [F2] Proper mixed cohomology and its weight bound are supplied by [[thm-proper-cohomology-has-functorial-mixed-hodge-weights-at-most-degree]], and the Cech descent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(C_p,\mathbb Q)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(C,\mathbb Q)$ by [[thm-proper-hypercovers-compute-constructible-derived-cohomology]] applied to the bounded proper hypercover $C_\bullet\to C$ of the normalization. Step 1.1 (the degree-one Cech computation). The degree-$p$ term of the Cech nerve of $\nu$ has underlying space the diagonal copy of $\mathbb P^1$ together with $2^{p+1}-2$ isolated points coming from the nonconstant tuples in $\{a,b\}^{p+1}$; scheme-theoretic nilpotents in the fibre products do not change the underlying analytic space or constant-sheaf cohomology. On the degree-zero cohomology row, $C^0=\mathbb Q$ and $C^1=\mathbb Q_{\mathrm{diag}}\oplus\mathbb Q_{ab}\oplus\mathbb Q_{ba}$ with $\delta^0=0$; evaluating $\delta^1c$ on a constant triple forces $c_{\mathrm{diag}}=0$, and evaluating it on $(a,b,a)$ gives $c_{ba}+c_{ab}=0$. These two conditions make every triple evaluation vanish: triples with adjacent repetitions cancel their two off-diagonal terms, and alternating triples have opposite coefficients. Hence $E_2^{1,0}=\mathbb Q$. The other total-degree-one entry is $E_1^{0,1}=H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathbb Q)=0$ by [F1], and no higher differential can enter or leave $(1,0)$ in the first-quadrant spectral sequence. Therefore $H^1(C,\mathbb Q)$ is one-dimensional. Step 2.1 (weight zero). The degree-zero cohomology row is pure of type $(0,0)$; by [F2] the $E_2^{1,0}$ term is the weight-zero graded piece of $H^1(C,\mathbb Q)$, and by Step 1.1 it is the only nonzero graded piece. Hence the whole one-dimensional space is pure of weight $0$ and type $(0,0)$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]), as asserted. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

statement: For $U=\mathbb C^\times\subset\mathbb P^1$, $H^1(U,\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q(-1)$, of weight $2$ and type $(1,1)$. In particular its weight is strictly larger than its cohomological degree.
strategy:
Direct finite verification of the logarithmic weight conventions on the punctured line.
Step 1. $U=\mathbb C^\times$ retracts onto a circle, so [[cor-homology-of-spheres]] and [[cor-cohomology-over-a-field-is-dual-to-homology-over-that-field]] give $H^1(U,\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$, generated under the logarithmic comparison of [[thm-logarithmic-complex-constructs-smooth-open-mixed-hodge-structures]] by $(2\pi i)^{-1}dz/z$; its residues at $0$ and $\infty$ are $1$ and $-1$.
Step 2. In the weight spectral sequence of the theorem for the SNC compactification $\mathbb P^1=\mathbb C^\times\sqcup\{0,\infty\}$, the weight-one column is $H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathbb Q)=0$ and the only possible nonzero contribution to $H^1(U)$ is the weight-two column $H^0(D,\mathbb Q)(-1)=\mathbb Q(-1)^{\oplus2}$, whose Gysin differential adds the two residue coordinates into $H^2(\mathbb P^1,\mathbb Q)$; its kernel is the line spanned by $(1,-1)$. Hence the unique degree-one class spans a copy of $\mathbb Q(-1)$, no other weight occurs, and the type is $(1,1)$.
Step 3. Conclude weight $2=1+1>1=n$ and type $(1,1)$, using the weight, type and Tate-twist conventions of [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]].
Obligations. The example is a leaf of the B page and nothing depends on it; its only non-published supplier is the logarithmic theorem, so it is blocked exactly when that theorem is.

statement: Every morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures is strict for $W$ and for $F$: $$f(W_nH)=f(H)\cap W_nK,\qquad f(F^pH_{\mathbb C})=f(H_{\mathbb C})\cap F^pK_{\mathbb C}$$ for all $n,p$. Its kernel, image and cokernel, with the induced or quotient filtrations, are mixed Hodge structures; the functor $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ is exact; and a morphism from a structure of weights at least $n$ (that is $W_{n-1}H=0$) to a structure of weights at most $n$ (that is $W_nK=K$) has pure image of weight $n$.
strategy: Apply the Deligne splitting lemma to $H$ and to $K$. Step 1: weight strictness. Let $y=f(x)\in f(H)\cap W_mK$ and decompose $x=\sum_{p,q}x^{p,q}$ and $y=\sum_{p,q}f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})$ along the splittings; functoriality of the splitting puts $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})$ in $I^{p,q}(K)$, so the displayed decompositions are the ones supplied by the lemma. As $y\in W_mK$ means $f_{\mathbb C}(x^{p,q})=0$ whenever $p+q>m$, one has $y=f(\sum_{p+q\le m}x^{p,q})$ with $\sum_{p+q\le m}x^{p,q}\in W_mH$. Step 2: Hodge strictness is the same computation with the condition $p<a$ instead of $p+q>m$: an element of $f(H_{\mathbb C})\cap F^aK_{\mathbb C}$ is the image of the sum of the $I^{p,q}$-components with $p\ge a$, which lies in $F^aH_{\mathbb C}$. Step 3: the rational equality follows from the complex one because both sides are complexifications of rational subspaces and the comparison maps are isomorphisms. Step 4: kernel, image and cokernel. The kernel and image are compatible with the bigraded decompositions: on each $\operatorname{Gr}^W_m$ the induced or quotient filtration is the restriction or quotient of the $(p,q)$-bigrading $H^{p,q}_m$, and a subspace or quotient of an $m$-opposed pair that is compatible with the bigrading is again $m$-opposed, with the conjugate of the $(p,q)$-piece equal to the $(q,p)$-piece; this is the argument of Deligne II 1.2.12 and 2.3.5(ii). Hence the induced and quotient filtrations satisfy the mixed Hodge axioms, and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ is exact because it is exact on each weight level by weight strictness. Step 5: the pure-image statement: if $W_{n-1}H=0$ and $W_nK=K$, then $W_{n-1}\operatorname{im}f=f(W_{n-1}H)=0$ and $W_n\operatorname{im}f=\operatorname{im}f\cap W_nK=\operatorname{im}f$, so the image is pure of weight $n$. The statement deliberately claims no splitting or uniqueness of the induced structures.

statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation ([[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]]) on a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety $S$. For each base point $s$, the monodromy-invariant space $H_s^{\pi_1(S,s)}$ ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]) is a Hodge substructure of $H_s$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]), and parallel transport identifies these spaces as one constant Hodge structure. Equivalently, the Hodge components of every global flat section are global flat sections. For $H=R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ with $f:X\to S$ smooth projective and an SNC smooth projective compactification $\overline X$ of $X$, the image of $H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ is exactly the invariant space.
strategy: Assume AC. Case H=R^mf_*Q first. (1) A relatively ample bundle gives a morphism Rf_*Q -> Rf_*Q[2] whose fibre maps are hard Lefschetz isomorphisms by [[thm-kahler-identities-give-lefschetz-sl-two-and-hard-lefschetz]]; the abstract splitting criterion [[lem-hard-lefschetz-splits-a-bounded-t-structure-complex]] then writes Rf_*Q as the sum of its shifted cohomology sheaves, so the Leray spectral sequence degenerates and its edge map H^m(X,Q) -> H^0(S,R^mf_*Q) is surjective; evaluation at s identifies H^0(S,R^mf_*Q) with the monodromy invariants of the fibre and is injective, with the fibre identified with H^m(X_s,Q) by proper base change [[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]]. (2) Choose an SNC compactification (existence [[lem-smooth-quasiprojective-varieties-admit-snc-projective-compactifications]]) and let X=overline X minus the boundary divisor; the logarithmic mixed Hodge theorem [[thm-logarithmic-complex-constructs-smooth-open-mixed-hodge-structures]] gives W_mH^m(X)=im(H^m(overline X)->H^m(X)). Restriction H^m(X)->H^m(X_s) has pure weight-m target, so by strictness [[lem-morphisms-of-mixed-hodge-structures-are-strict]] its image is the image of W_mH^m(X), hence of H^m(overline X); step (1) identifies the same image with the invariants, and the compactification-independence clause of the logarithmic theorem makes this independent of the chosen SNC model, so the assertion is stated for SNC smooth projective compactifications of X, exactly the class for which the weight formula is proved and whose existence the cited lemma supplies. (3) The induced constant structure on H^0(S,H) is independent of s because the kernel of the restriction is independent of s and the quotient carries the quotient Hodge structure; Tate twists and finite sums preserve this. (4) On the dense realization open U a flat Hodge idempotent sends the fixed Hodge structure of the ambient sum to a fixed Hodge substructure of H|_U, and the flat sections over U are exactly those over S by the fundamental-group surjectivity of [[lem-algebraic-open-inclusion-surjects-on-fundamental-groups]]; each Hodge component of a flat section over S is flat on U, agrees on a dense subset of every simply connected ball in S with a flat vector, hence agrees on the ball by continuity. The family and lattice suppliers are [[lem-smooth-projective-morphisms-give-polarizable-rational-gauss-manin-variations]]. No analytic-variation theorem for punctured discs is imported.

statement:
Assume AC. Let $U$ be smooth quasiprojective over $\mathbb C$, and choose an SNC smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, boundary $D$. The logarithmic de Rham complex with Hodge filtration by degree and pole-count weight filtration constructs a functorial rational mixed Hodge structure on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$, independent of the compactification. Its weights are at least $n$, and
$$W_nH^n(U,\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H^n(U,\mathbb Q)).$$
strategy:
Route (Deligne, Théorie de Hodge II, 3.1-3.2: the logarithmic de Rham complex, its residue/weight-graded description, and the mixed Hodge structure on the cohomology of the complement of an SNC divisor).
Step 1 (the filtered logarithmic complex). In coordinates with $D=\{z_1\cdots z_r=0\}$ define $\Omega^\bullet_X(\log D)$ as the exterior algebra of $dz_1/z_1,\dots,dz_r/z_r,dz_{r+1},\dots,dz_d$ with holomorphic coefficients; its differential preserves pole count. Let $W_a$ be the subcomplex of forms with at most $a$ logarithmic factors ($W_a=0$ for $a<0$) and $F^p$ the forms of degree at least $p$. Residues along the components give $\operatorname{Gr}^W_a\Omega^\bullet_X(\log D)\cong\Omega^\bullet_{D^{[a]}}[-a]$, where $D^{[a]}$ is the disjoint union of the $a$-fold component intersections; a changed local equation is a unit times the old one and $d\log(uz)=d\log z+d\log u$ changes only the lower pole-count term, so the residue is well defined ([given, construct, algebra]).
Step 2 (local computation). On a polydisc the complement of the coordinate hyperplanes retracts to $(S^1)^r$; with the Künneth isomorphism for finite free homology ([[thm-cohomological-kunneth-isomorphism-under-finite-free-hypotheses]]), the sphere homology ([[cor-homology-of-spheres]]) and field duality ([[cor-cohomology-over-a-field-is-dual-to-homology-over-that-field]]) its rational cohomology is the exterior algebra on the coordinate meridians. Expanding holomorphic coefficients in convergent power series and integrating monomials shows that $z_i\partial/\partial z_i$ is invertible on every nonzero exponent (division by a positive integer preserves local convergence) and ordinary integration contracts the remaining coordinates; only the zero-exponent logarithmic wedges survive, so $\Omega^\bullet_X(\log D)$ computes $Rj_*\mathbb C_U$ after complexification of the rational comparison, and pole count on its cohomology sheaves is the filtration $\tau_{\le a}Rj_*\mathbb Q_U$. Integrating a meridian gives $2\pi i$, so the rational residue comparison is $\mathbb Q_{D^{[a]}}(-a)[-a]$. This analysis is written out, not cited from an unfiltered de Rham comparison; the sheaf/singular comparison on $U$ uses [[lem-locally-contractible-metric-spaces-have-singular-constant-sheaf-cohomology]].
Step 3 (mixed Hodge complex). The compactification X and each component of each SNC intersection stratum D^[a] are smooth projective over C; closed intersections remain projective, and components of differing dimensions are handled separately. Apply [[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]] to each pure-dimensional component: its analytification is a compact Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold with a positive closed real (1,1)-form representing an ample rational class. Thus [[thm-compact-kahler-hodge-decomposition-via-elliptic-harmonic-forms]] applies and supplies the functorial rational pure Hodge structures, the holomorphic-degree Hodge filtration and its E1 degeneration. In particular H^{k-a}(D^[a],Q)(-a) is pure of weight (k-a)+2a=k+a. With the residue and rational comparison of Steps1-2, the weight-graded complexes satisfy exactly [[def-cohomological-mixed-hodge-complex]], so [[lem-mixed-hodge-complexes-give-functorial-cohomology-and-simplicial-weights]] gives the functorial rational mixed Hodge structure on H^n(U,Q) and the shifted cohomology weight filtration. No absolute hard Lefschetz, Hodge-Riemann package, relative decomposition or analytic-local-system semisimplicity is required by this step.
Step 4 (weights at least $n$ and the image formula). In the weight spectral sequence $E_1^{-a,q}=H^{q-2a}(D^{[a]},\mathbb Q)(-a)\Longrightarrow H^{q-a}(U,\mathbb Q)$ only $a\ge0$ occurs, and the degree-$n$ total $q=n+a$ has weight at least $n$. The column $a=0$ is $H^n(X)$ and admits no outgoing differential to a lower column, so its contribution is exactly the image of $H^n(X)\to H^n(U)$, which is $W_nH^n(U)$ by the shifted filtration formula since $W_0=\Omega^\bullet_X$ ([step 1, step 3, algebra]).
Step 5 (functoriality and independence of the compactification). Pullback along a morphism of compactified pairs preserves logarithmic forms, degree and pole count (a boundary equation pulls back to a unit times a product of boundary equations with nonnegative exponents, so its logarithmic differential is the corresponding linear combination modulo a regular form) and commutes with rational comparison, hence induces a morphism of mixed Hodge structures on open cohomology. The graph/domination construction of [[lem-smooth-quasiprojective-varieties-admit-snc-projective-compactifications]] extends arbitrary open morphisms to compactified pairs and dominates two compactifications by a third; the comparison map on open cohomology is the identity, and strictness of mixed Hodge morphisms ([[lem-morphisms-of-mixed-hodge-structures-are-strict]]) makes it an isomorphism of mixed Hodge structures, so the filtrations and the MHS are independent of choices. For a smooth projective compactification whose boundary is not SNC, dominate it by an SNC modification and use [[lem-smooth-projective-modification-preserves-open-cohomology-images]] to identify the two restriction images and obtain the same $W_n$ formula. This last step is where [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]] is needed for the vocabulary (weights, type, Tate twists) used throughout.
Planning prerequisite correction (round1): the exact analytification supplier is now declared directly, and the logarithmic A page requires its earlier projective-Hodge home after the guarded1811/1812 and1815/1816 order exchange. This resolves the identified prerequisite placement only; complete authored supplier and consumer proofs remain owed to the ordinary native proof/review stages.
Obligations for the Step-3 author. (a) Write out the residue isomorphism and its sign/differential conventions, the polydisc computation and the rational ($2\pi i$-)normalization in full. (b) The E1 degeneracy must be derived from the cited smooth projective Hodge theory, not from a bare citation to Deligne; state the functoriality of the pure Hodge structures under the inclusions $D^{[a]}\hookrightarrow X$ used for the comparison maps. (c) Do not use the MHS on $H^n(X)$ to prove purity of $H^*(D^{[a]})$; the strata inputs are separate. (d) AC is consumed through the compact Kähler, resolution, duality and sheaf-cohomology suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]); the log-complex algebra itself is choice-free.

statement: Assume AC. Let $U$ be smooth quasiprojective over $\mathbb C$, let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be any smooth projective compactification, and let $g:Y\to U$ be a morphism with $Y$ proper (possibly singular and reducible). Then, in every degree $n$, $$\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{(jg)^*}H^n(Y,\mathbb Q))=\operatorname{im}(H^n(U,\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{g^*}H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)).$$ Both images are pure Hodge substructures of weight $n$. This includes the restriction of a smooth projective total space to a proper singular fibre through an open subvariety, which is the exact use in de Cataldo-Migliorini Proposition 8.3.2.
strategy: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Source: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge III, (8.2.6) with its proof (printed p. 39), which reduces to the strictness input (3.2.17) of Theorie de Hodge II; both read in full. [F1] [[thm-logarithmic-complex-constructs-smooth-open-mixed-hodge-structures]]: the logarithmic mixed Hodge structure on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$ satisfies $W_{n-1}H^n(U)=0$ and $W_nH^n(U)=\operatorname{im}j^*$ for any smooth projective compactification $j$. [F2] [[thm-proper-cohomology-has-functorial-mixed-hodge-weights-at-most-degree]]: $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ carries a mixed Hodge structure with $W_nH^n(Y)=H^n(Y)$, and the pullback $g^*:H^n(U)\to H^n(Y)$ is a mixed Hodge morphism for the logarithmic structure on $U$, including the case of a morphism from a smooth open variety into a proper variety. [F3] [[lem-morphisms-of-mixed-hodge-structures-are-strict]]: every mixed Hodge morphism is strict for $W$, so $g^*(W_nH^n(U))=\operatorname{im}g^*\cap W_nH^n(Y)$, and the image of a morphism from a structure of weights at least $n$ to one of weights at most $n$ is pure of weight $n$. Step 1.1 (equality of subspaces). By [F3] applied to the morphism $g^*$, $g^*(W_nH^n(U))=\operatorname{im}g^*\cap W_nH^n(Y)$; by [F2] this intersection is $\operatorname{im}g^*$. By [F1] the left-hand side is $g^*(\operatorname{im}j^*)=\operatorname{im}(g^*j^*)=\operatorname{im}((jg)^*)$, so the two images agree as actual subspaces of $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$, without choosing a splitting of the weight filtration on $H^n(U)$. Step 2.1 (purity of the image). Put $I=\operatorname{im}g^*$. Strictness [F3] gives $W_{n-1}I=g^*(W_{n-1}H^n(U))=0$ by [F1], while [F2] gives $W_nI=I$. Hence the induced mixed Hodge structure ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]) on $I$ is pure of weight $n$, and the same holds for the equal image of $(jg)^*$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

statement: Assume AC. The rational cohomology $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ of every proper complex algebraic variety has a functorial mixed Hodge structure with weights at most $n$. For a morphism $g:Y\to U$ with $Y$ proper and $U$ smooth quasiprojective, its pullback $H^n(U)\to H^n(Y)$ is a mixed Hodge morphism for the logarithmic structure on $U$. If $Y\to X$ is proper with $X$ smooth projective of dimension $d$, the proper homological class map $$H_i^{\mathrm{BM}}(Y,\mathbb Q)=H_i(Y,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbb Q)(d)$$ is a mixed Hodge morphism after the indicated Tate twist. Its image, and consequently the untwisted image in $H^{2d-i}(X)$, is a pure Hodge substructure. No smoothness of $Y$ is assumed.
strategy: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Sources: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge III, (8.2.1)-(8.2.4) (mixed Hodge structure on $H^*(X)$ via a proper hypercover of a separated finite-type scheme, independence of the diagram, functoriality, and the weight bounds for proper $X$; printed pp. 38-39) and Andrzej Weber, Notes on Mixed Hodge Structures, (4.3.1)-(4.3.3) (the mixed Hodge complex of a smooth compact simplicial variety, its induced structure on $H^*(X)$ and the weight spectral sequence; printed pp. 10-11). [F1] Smooth projective hyperresolutions and their common refinements are [[thm-proper-varieties-admit-smooth-projective-hyperresolutions]]. [F2] Their ordinary constant-coefficient cohomological descent is [[thm-proper-hypercovers-compute-constructible-derived-cohomology]]; for the constant rational complex in degree zero the internal lower bound is $a=0$, so every diagonal is finite. [F3] [[thm-compact-kahler-hodge-decomposition-via-elliptic-harmonic-forms]]: a smooth projective complex variety $V$ has $H^q(V,\mathbb Q)$ pure of weight $q$, with functorial rational structure, strict Hodge filtration and pullback preserving type. [F4] [[lem-mixed-hodge-complexes-give-functorial-cohomology-and-simplicial-weights]] (ii): a cosimplicial system of weight-zero rational Hodge complexes concentrated in nonnegative bidegrees, with $H^q(K^p)$ pure of weight $q$, has a simple complex that is a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex for the filtration by cosimplicial degree, with $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n$ computed from the weight spectral sequence; [[def-cohomological-mixed-hodge-complex]] and [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]] fix the vocabulary. [F5] The singular comparison on $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ uses [[lem-locally-contractible-metric-spaces-have-singular-constant-sheaf-cohomology]] after verifying its hypotheses in Step 3.1; strictness of mixed Hodge morphisms is [[lem-morphisms-of-mixed-hodge-structures-are-strict]]. [F6] [[thm-logarithmic-complex-constructs-smooth-open-mixed-hodge-structures]] and Step 5.1 give the smooth-open pullback clause; ordinary duality inputs are [[thm-poincare-duality-for-oriented-topological-manifolds]], [[cor-cohomology-over-a-field-is-dual-to-homology-over-that-field]] and [[prop-cap-product-naturality-and-projection-formula]]. Step 1.1 (cosimplicial Hodge complex). Choose a smooth projective hyperresolution $Y_\bullet\to Y$ and resolve the constant rational sheaf and the holomorphic de Rham complex functorially on it, so derived global sections form a cosimplicial comparison system; every term is a weight-zero Hodge complex whose degree-$q$ cohomology is smooth projective cohomology, pure of weight $q$ by [F3]. By [F4] the simple complex is a cohomological mixed Hodge complex, descent [F2] identifies its cohomology with the derived constant-sheaf cohomology of $Y$, and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n$ is computed by the $E_2$ page with $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(Y_p,\mathbb Q)$. Since $p=n-q\ge0$ on the relevant diagonals, all weights are at most $n$; diagonals are finite by [F2]. Step 2.1 (finiteness and functoriality of the structure). Each cohomology group is finite-dimensional because only finitely many smooth projective terms contribute in each degree. For a second hyperresolution, common refinement induces filtered comparison maps on the simple complexes whose induced map on ordinary cohomology is the identity; strictness [F5] upgrades it to an isomorphism, so the structure is independent of the resolution. A lift of a morphism of proper varieties to hypercovers, as supplied by [F1], gives a filtered pullback whose induced cohomology map is the canonical one; hence proper pullbacks are mixed Hodge morphisms. Step 3.1 (singular comparison and metrization of $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$). In the analytic topology of [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]], $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ is compact (a surjective continuous image of the compact $Y_0^{\mathrm{an}}$) and Hausdorff (separatedness makes the diagonal closed). Choose a finite atlas by affine open charts: each chart is quasi-projective, so [[thm-constructible-sheaves-admit-finite-stratified-triangulations-and-finite-local-cohomology]] provides a finite triangulation of it, and [[lem-finite-simplicial-open-stars-have-explicit-conical-product-charts]] shows that open stars of simplices form a basis of contractible open sets; these inherit to $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$. Metrizability follows from [[thm-a-compact-hausdorff-space-is-regular-and-normal]], [[cor-compact-hausdorff-partitions-of-unity]] and [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]: compactness gives a finite cover by smaller chart neighbourhoods whose closures lie in the charts, a subordinate finite partition of unity provides compactly supported continuous cutoff functions, and the map that records the cutoffs together with the cutoff-weighted affine coordinates is a continuous injection of the compact space into Euclidean space, hence an embedding. The comparison lemma [F5] then identifies the cohomology of Step 1.1 with ordinary singular cohomology $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$, carrying the finite-dimensional mixed Hodge structure. Step 4.1 (pullback from a smooth open). Let $g:Y\to U$ with $j:U\hookrightarrow\overline U$ an SNC smooth projective compactification supplied with [[thm-logarithmic-complex-constructs-smooth-open-mixed-hodge-structures]]. Pullback sends logarithmic forms on $\overline U$ to regular forms on each smooth projective $Y_p$ because the boundary divisor pulls back to the complement of the image of $Y_p$ in $U$; it preserves the Hodge filtration and maps the pole-count weight filtration into the weight-zero ordinary de Rham complex of $Y_p$, since negative pole counts vanish. Choosing functorial resolutions so that equal composites act equally makes these pullbacks a single chain map from the logarithmic complex into the simplicial simple complex, supported in simplicial degree zero with alternating face differential zero. It is therefore a morphism of mixed Hodge complexes and induces the actual map $g^*$ as a mixed Hodge morphism. Step 5.1 (homological class map). For proper $Y$ ordinary and Borel-Moore homology coincide, and [[cor-cohomology-over-a-field-is-dual-to-homology-over-that-field]] together with finite-dimensionality identifies $H_i(Y,\mathbb Q)$ with the dual of $H^i(Y,\mathbb Q)$; with the dual conventions of [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]] this dual has weights at least $-i$, because $H^i(Y,\mathbb Q)$ has weights at most $i$. The homological pushforward $H_i(Y)\to H_i(X)$ is dual to the pullback of Step 2.1, hence a mixed Hodge morphism, and Poincare duality on the smooth projective $X$ of dimension $d$ identifies $H_i(X,\mathbb Q)$ with $H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbb Q)(d)$, a pure structure of weight $-i$, since the cup product pairs complementary types and the trace has type $(d,d)$. The composite is a mixed Hodge morphism from a structure of weights at least $-i$ to one of weights at most $-i$, so by strictness [F5] its image is pure of weight $-i$; untwisting by the inverse Tate twist returns it to $H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbb Q)$ as a pure Hodge substructure. statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The finite étale morphism $f:\mathbb C^\times\to\mathbb C^\times$, $z\mapsto z^r$, for $r\ge1$, gives a rank-$r$ geometric pure weight-zero local system $R^0f_*\mathbb Q$ ([[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]], [[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]). Its monodromy cyclically permutes the $r$ sheets and its complexification is a direct sum of one-dimensional root-of-unity characters ([[def-roots-of-unity-in-a-field]]).
strategy: Verification. (1) The graph of z^r=tW^r is closed in C^× x P^1 and the derivative rz^{r-1} is nonzero on the source, so f is a smooth projective (indeed finite étale) morphism by [[thm-jacobian-criterion-smooth-morphism]]; each fibre is r points, so R^0f_*Q has rank r with the sheet-indicator basis of type (0,0), and the ordinary dot product in that basis is a flat rational positive polarization. (2) A positive generator of pi_1(C^×) multiplies a chosen root by e^{2*pi*i/r}, cyclically permuting the sheets. (3) Over C the vectors v_j=sum_a e^{-2*pi*i*j*a/r} e_a are eigenvectors of the cyclic permutation with the r distinct r-th-root eigenvalues, so the Fourier matrix is invertible and the complexification splits as a direct sum of rank-one characters; the characters are distinct, so the module is semisimple ([[def-semisimple-module]]). (4) The geometric semisimplicity theorem [[thm-smooth-projective-gauss-manin-local-systems-are-semisimple]] gives the same semisimplicity over every characteristic-zero field, including fields not containing all r-th roots.

statement: (i) Let $K$ be a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex. Then for every $n$ the vector space $H^n(K_{\mathbb Q})$ carries a mixed Hodge structure whose weight filtration is the shifted image filtration $W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K))$ and whose Hodge filtration is the image filtration $F^pH^n(K_{\mathbb C})=\operatorname{im}(H^n(F^pK_{\mathbb C})\to H^n(K_{\mathbb C}))$. In the weight spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-p}K)$ one has $E_1^{p,q}$ pure of weight $q$, the sequence degenerates at $E_2$, and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n(K)\cong E_2^{n-m,m}$ compatibly with the Hodge filtrations. A morphism of cohomological mixed Hodge complexes induces, on every $H^n$, a morphism of the resulting mixed Hodge structures. (ii) Let $K^\bullet$ be a cosimplicial system of weight-zero rational Hodge complexes concentrated in nonnegative cohomological degrees, i.e. cochain complexes $K^{p,q}$ with coface maps and an internal differential satisfying the cosimplicial identities, with $K^{p,q}=0$ unless $p,q\ge0$, and with $H^q(K^p)$ a pure Hodge structure of weight $q$ for all $p,q$. Form its simple complex $sK$ with the standard total differential and the increasing filtration $L$ by cosimplicial degree, $L_{-p}sK^n=\bigoplus_{i\ge p}K^{i,n-i}$. Then $sK$ is a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex for the filtration $L$ and the Hodge filtrations of the $K^p$, the cosimplicial spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(K^p)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(sK)$ degenerates at $E_2$, and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$; consequently all weights of $H^n(sK)$ are at most $n$.
strategy:
Route: Deligne III Scholie (8.1.9) and Theorem (8.1.15), transferred with the cohomological filtered-complex construction. Step 1 (weight spectral sequence). Apply the published cohomological filtered complex construction to $K$ with the decreasing filtration $F_{\mathrm{wt}}^p:=W_{-p}K$, which is degreewise finite by the definition. Its first page is $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^pK)=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-p}K)$; the axiom of the mixed Hodge complex makes this a pure Hodge structure of weight $(p+q)+(-p)=q$ with its induced $F$, and its abutment is the image filtration $F^p_{\mathrm{wt}}H^n=\operatorname{im}(H^n(W_{-p}K))$, i.e. $W_mH^n$ under the shift $m=n-p$. Step 2 (degeneration at $E_2$). The differentials $d_r$ are induced by the differentials of the complex, so they preserve the rational structure and $F$; hence each $d_r$ is a morphism of the pure Hodge structures on the pages. By Step 1 and induction, $E_r^{p,q}$ is pure of weight $q$ for all $r\ge1$: $d_1$ is a morphism between pure structures of weight $q$ (in $E_1^{p,q}\to E_1^{p+1,q}$ both second indices are $q$), so its kernel and image are pure of weight $q$ by the strictness lemma, and $E_2^{p,q}=\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_1$ is pure of weight $q$. For $r\ge2$ the target $E_r^{p+r,q-r+1}$ has weight $q-r+1<q$, and a morphism of mixed Hodge structures cannot map a pure weight-$q$ structure to a pure weight-$(q-r+1)$ structure (their weight filtrations force the image into $W_{q-r+1}$ of the target, which is zero); hence every $d_r$, $r\ge2$, vanishes and the sequence stabilizes at $E_2$. Step 3 (filtration identification). The abutment isomorphism $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n\cong E_\infty^{n-m,m}$ of Step 1 identifies complexes of vector spaces; the $F$-filtrations agree as well. For this, correct representatives: a class of $F^pH^n$ has a representative in $F^pK^n$; its image in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mK$ is a cycle in $F^p$, and the obstruction to lifting it to a cycle of $F^pK^n\cap W_mK^n$ is its differential, which lies in the image of $d$ and in $F^p$; strictness of the differential on the next lower weight-graded piece supplies a correction in $F^p$, and finiteness of $W$ terminates the descent. The construction is compatible with the page filtration because all $d_r$ are strict for $F$ on the relevant pages (they are morphisms of pure Hodge structures, using the strictness lemma), so the recursive filtration on the stable page is the one induced from the complex. Step 4 (functoriality). A morphism of mixed Hodge complexes preserves both filtrations and the comparison, so the induced map on $H^n$ preserves the image filtrations and is a mixed Hodge morphism by definition. Step 5 (cosimplicial case). The simple complex of the cosimplicial system is the total complex of the associated first-quadrant cochain bicomplex; the cosimplicial identities make the total differential square to zero and give $\operatorname{Gr}^L_{-p}(sK)\cong K^p[-p]$, and the filtration $L$ is finite in each degree because $p,q\ge0$ force $0\le p\le n$ in degree $n$. By hypothesis $H^q(K^p)$ is pure of weight $q$, so $H^n(\operatorname{Gr}^L_{-p}sK)=H^{n-p}(K^p)$ is pure of weight $n-p=n+(-p)$: the axiom of the mixed Hodge complex holds with filtration index $-p$, and Step 1 applies with $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(K^p)$. Setting $q:=m$ gives $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$, and $q=n-p\le n$ because $p\ge0$. The construction of the simple complex is carried inside this proof; no separate cosimplicial totalization
supplier is assumed. The comparison map of sK is a filtered quasi-isomorphism because the filtration is
finite in each total degree and on each graded piece Gr^L_{-p}sK = K^p[-p] it is the given levelwise
filtered comparison, so the finite-filtration induction on the two-term filtrations applies; the internal
differential on each K^p is F-strict by the weight-zero Hodge complex hypothesis. Nothing in Steps 1-5
uses a choice principle or a splitting of the filtration.

statement:
Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of complex projective varieties, with $X$ smooth connected of dimension $n$, let $\eta$ be a very ample source class, and put $L=f^*c_1(B)$ for a very ample target line $B$. Write $K=Rf_*\mathbb Q_X[n]$, $P_b={}^pH^bK$, $F_bH^q(X)=\operatorname{im}(H^{q-n}(Y,{}^p\tau_{\le b}K)\to H^q(X))$, $H_b^q=F_bH^q/F_{b-1}H^q$, $m=\dim f(X)$ and

$$r(f)=\max_i\bigl(2i+\dim\{y:\dim f^{-1}(y)=i\}-n\bigr).$$

Consider the following package: relative $\eta$ hard Lefschetz $\eta^i:P_{-i}\simeq P_i$; a finite normalized splitting $K\simeq\bigoplus_bP_b[-b]$; semisimplicity of every $P_b$ with semisimple complexifications of its IC local systems; target graded hard Lefschetz $L^j:H_b^{n+b-j}\simeq H_b^{n+b+j}$; pure Hodge structures of their ordinary degree on the canonical graded groups; and polarized orthogonal double primitive decomposition. The double primitive space is

$$\mathcal P_{-i}^{-j}=\ker\eta^{i+1}\cap\ker L^{j+1}\subset H_{-i}^{n-i-j},\qquad i,j\ge0,$$

with polarization $Q_t(u,v)=(-1)^{t(t-1)/2}\int_X\eta^iL^ju\wedge v$, $t=n-i-j$, and positivity $Q_t(Cu,\bar u)>0$ for nonzero $u$, where $C$ acts on type $(p,q)$ by $i^{p-q}$. Filtration and primitive forms are the canonical graded ones; no primitive-compatible lift to ordinary global cohomology is assumed.

If this package holds for all smooth connected projective-source maps of lexicographically smaller pair $(r,m)$, with $r$ primary, then it holds for $f$. The image-dimension-zero base is supplied by absolute polarized Hodge theory and finite linear algebra. Finite disconnected smooth sources are handled componentwise. The statement preserves arbitrary projective fibres and requires neither semismallness nor affine paving.

Sources: de Cataldo and Migliorini, The Hodge theory of algebraic maps, arXiv:math/0306030 (final version), complete PDF, SS4.4 (cup product with a line bundle; Lemma 4.4.2, Theorem 4.4.4; PDF pp. 35-37), SS4.5-4.6 (weight filtrations, the sign in 4.5.2 and the graded groups; PDF pp. 37-39), SS4.7 (universal hyperplane section, defect $r(f)$, Propositions 4.7.4-4.7.9; PDF pp. 39-43), SS5.1-5.4 (Lemma 5.1.1, Propositions 5.1.3, 5.2.1-5.2.4, 5.3.1-5.3.2, Lemmas 5.4.1-5.4.4; PDF pp. 43-51) and SS6.1-6.4 (Propositions 6.2.2, 6.3.1-6.3.2, Theorem 6.4.2; PDF pp. 51-59), all read in full; BBD, Faisceaux pervers, 4.2.3-4.2.6.2 and 5.4.10-5.4.15 (PDF pp. 109-112, 145-148); Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, SS22-24 (PDF pp. 83-92). The complete ordered local constructions A-H of the authoring carrier are embedded for this item; the steps below are the exact assembled route. [F1] [[thm-ordinary-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]], [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]], [[thm-complex-algebraic-varieties-and-maps-admit-compatible-finite-stratifications]] supply perversity, coherent ordinary six operations and compatible finite Whitney strata, with exact noncharacteristic pullback [[lem-noncharacteristic-complex-stratified-pullback-is-perverse-exact]]. [F2] [[lem-affine-morphisms-have-one-sided-perverse-exactness]], [[lem-artin-affine-vanishing-for-constructible-perverse-sheaves]], [[lem-universal-hyperplane-relative-weak-lefschetz-and-maximal-pullback-subobjects]], [[lem-projective-hyperplane-sections-decrease-the-defect-of-semismallness]], [[thm-generic-smoothness-characteristic-zero]], [[thm-bertini-smooth-hyperplane-section]] and [[lem-projective-hypersurface-dimension-drop]] supply the affine one-sided exactness, vanishing, universal-hyperplane weak Lefschetz and defect drop. [F3] [[lem-pullback-of-the-thom-class-along-a-transverse-section]], [[prop-first-chern-class-of-tensor-dual-and-conjugate-lines]] and [[thm-top-chern-class-equals-euler-class-of-the-underlying-real-bundle]] fix the positive divisor Thom/cup comparison and the complex-line normalization $c_1(B)=e(B_{\mathbb R})$. [F4] [[thm-polarized-hodge-riemann-and-hard-lefschetz-for-smooth-projective-varieties]], [[lem-graded-hard-lefschetz-has-a-canonical-primitive-decomposition]], [[lem-nilpotent-lefschetz-filtration-is-canonical-and-self-dual]], [[lem-hard-lefschetz-splits-a-bounded-t-structure-complex]], [[lem-middle-lefschetz-primitive-polarization-follows-from-nonmiddle-polarizations]], [[lem-polarized-hodge-structures-have-orthogonal-semisimple-substructures]] and [[lem-perverse-closed-support-splitting-is-equivalent-to-costalk-stalk-isomorphism]] supply the absolute Hodge input, the graded/nilpotent splitting machinery, the middle limiting polarization and the supported splitting criterion. [F5] [[thm-mixed-hodge-weights-control-proper-cohomological-restriction-images]], [[thm-proper-cohomology-has-functorial-mixed-hodge-weights-at-most-degree]], [[thm-smooth-projective-gauss-manin-local-systems-are-semisimple]] and [[lem-algebraic-open-inclusion-surjects-on-fundamental-groups]] supply the proper restriction-image equality, the pure Hodge class image, geometric local-system semisimplicity and dense-open fundamental-group surjectivity. Step 1.1 (well-founded data and base case). The pair $(r(f),m)$ is nonnegative: on a generic fibre of dimension $a=n-m$ the contribution is $2a+m-n=a\ge0$, with finitely many fibre-dimension loci. If $m=0$ the package is absolute hard Lefschetz, ordinary truncation splitting, point semisimplicity and Hodge-Riemann; finite disconnected smooth sources are handled componentwise and empty sources give zero. Step 2.1 (Construction A). The universal evaluation section cuts a smooth divisor $D\subset X\times\mathbb P^\vee$ with class $\operatorname{pr}_X^*\eta+\operatorname{pr}_{\mathbb P}^*h$; the restriction-Gysin composite of the positive normal Thom counit is the line class, and tensor naturality with ${}^p\tau_{\le j}$ kills the degree-two parameter term on $(j\to j+2)$-perverse groups, so the composite with $\eta'^{r-1}$ is $\eta^r$. Step 3.1 (Construction C). For $r>0$ the universal map has smaller defect, its class $\eta'+h$ is absolutely ample and induces the same relative operator; the maximal pullback quotient forbids a kernel in $P_{-1}\xrightarrow{\eta}P_1$ and duality gives surjectivity; higher powers use outside weak-Lefschetz isomorphisms; for $r=0$ the fibre-dimension support bound and self-duality make $K$ perverse. The abstract bounded-$t$ splitting gives $K\simeq\bigoplus_bP_b[-b]$, and nonzero perverse degrees are split subquotients of lower-defect universal objects, so ordinary-heart full faithfulness descends their projectors and duality handles positive degrees, including the complexified local-system clause. Step 4.1 (Construction D). Graded $L$-hard Lefschetz outside perverse degree zero follows from fixed source cuts of positive defect; in degree zero target-cut restriction/Gysin isomorphisms give powers $\ge2$, and the first power follows by lifting a kernel to an ordinary $L$-kernel through the strict block-diagonal action and contradicting a nonzero middle primitive with positive lower-map Hodge-Riemann norm against a vanishing target Thom-cup integral. Step 5.1 (Construction E). The intrinsic centered filtration identifies the perverse filtration degree by degree and proves it Hodge; nonmiddle double primitives restrict to lower source/target slices and their forms are identified with lower Hodge-Riemann polarizations; hypotheses (a)-(c) of [[lem-middle-lefschetz-primitive-polarization-follows-from-nonmiddle-polarizations]] are verified, including well-definedness of the graded forms and the middle subspace identification, giving the $(0,0)$ positivity. Step 6.1 (Construction F). The zero-stratum costalk/stalk map is identified with the degree-zero graded refined intersection map $H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{n,0}(Z)\to H^n_0(Z)$; Artin vanishing on an affine target open gives graded restriction surjectivity, the proper mixed-Hodge image equality upgrades it to global surjectivity using strictness from the finite normalized splitting, proper trace duality gives injectivity of the class map, and the canonical perverse $\eta$ projectors decompose the pure class image into orthogonal primitive blocks whose sign-adjusted polarizations restrict nondegenerately by [[lem-polarized-hodge-structures-have-orthogonal-semisimple-substructures]]; hence the intersection matrix is invertible. Step 7.1 (Construction G). Projective target slices through an arbitrary positive-dimensional stratum point are built by constrained Bertini, giving lower slices with the actual local costalk/stalk isomorphism at every stratum; the formal closed-support criterion [[lem-perverse-closed-support-splitting-is-equivalent-to-costalk-stalk-isomorphism]] then inducts over the finite closed-stratum frontier and yields the IC decomposition of $P_0$ before local-system semisimplicity is used. Step 8.1 (Construction H). The moving hyperplane family $\mathcal X_T\to T$ has a good algebraic section by a rational point in an explicit product-projective generic fibre, the graph factorization has net perverse shift $(d-s)+s-d=0$, the fibre stalk map is the (surjective) lower-map global graded restriction, and Gauss-Manin semisimplicity plus dense-open fundamental-group surjectivity transport rational and complexified semisimplicity to each stratum; the top stratum is $R^{n-m}f_*\mathbb Q$ and zero strata are finite vector spaces. Intermediate extension gives the finite IC sums. Step 9.1 (assembly). Steps 1.1-8.1 prove every clause of the package for $f$ from the package for all lexicographically smaller smooth connected projective-source pairs, with $r$ primary; every auxiliary source slice, universal family or target slice used is strictly lower and step 1.1 supplies the image-zero base, so the induction step is complete. Arbitrary projective fibres and singular proper images are preserved; no semismallness, affine paving, finite-ADE or arithmetic purity enters. statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For a smooth projective morphism $f:X\to S$ of smooth quasiprojective complex varieties, $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ is a finite-rank local system ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]), with full monodromy-stable integral lattice obtained from $R^mf_*\mathbb Z$ modulo torsion, and with a continuous pure Hodge decomposition of weight $m$ ([[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]]). A relatively ample line bundle supplies flat Lefschetz operators and a flat rational polarization of this variation. Products, sums, Tate twists, exterior powers and Hodge direct summands have the corresponding geometric realizations and full integral lattices. Pullbacks of algebraic maps between smooth projective fibers preserve rational Hodge structures.
strategy: Assume AC. Route: local fibration and finite generation, then harmonic comparison, then flatness of the polarization. (1) By the Jacobian criterion [[thm-jacobian-criterion-smooth-morphism]] the analytification is a submersion; projectivity makes it proper, so it is a locally trivial smooth fibre bundle with compact fibres; horizontal lifting of radial paths in coordinate balls gives the rational and integral cohomology local systems. [[lem-locally-contractible-metric-spaces-have-singular-constant-sheaf-cohomology]] identifies singular cohomology with constant-sheaf cohomology on the fibres and local product neighbourhoods, and proper base change in [[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]] identifies these with the cohomology sheaves $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$. Finite CW models of the fibres ([[lem-a-closed-smooth-manifold-has-the-homotopy-type-of-a-finite-cw-complex]]) make the integral groups finitely generated, and quotienting torsion gives a full lattice. (2) Relative Kähler metrics from a projective embedding give a smooth family of elliptic Laplacians on a fixed compact model; a fixed spectral contour and the Neumann series for the resolvent give continuously varying finite-rank harmonic projections, and the Hodge type decomposition is invariant, giving the continuous pure Hodge decomposition by harmonic representatives through [[thm-compact-kahler-hodge-decomposition-via-elliptic-harmonic-forms]]. (3) The first Chern class of the relatively ample bundle is the restriction of a global class, hence a flat Lefschetz operator, and cup product with it is compatible with the flat transport; Hodge-Riemann ([[thm-hodge-riemann-bilinear-relations-for-smooth-projective-varieties]]) makes the primitive polarization flat, and the sign-adjusted full-cohomology polarization is obtained from the flat primitive Lefschetz decomposition. (4) Products, disjoint unions, Tate twists, exterior powers and prescribed Hodge direct summands are realized by product families and Künneth ([[thm-cohomological-kunneth-isomorphism-under-finite-free-hypotheses]]), disjoint unions, the flat projector, and the rational alternating idempotent; intersecting rational summands with the ambient full lattice and clearing denominators gives their full lattices; algebraic pullbacks preserve Hodge types. This is the family argument, not an imported Gauss-Manin semisimplicity theorem.

statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If $f:X\to S$ is smooth projective with $S$ a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety, then every local system $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]) is semisimple over $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-semisimple-module]]) and remains semisimple after scalar extension to every characteristic-zero field. More generally the complex local system of every geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation is semisimple. The algebraic realization and geometric integral lattice are essential hypotheses; no claim is made for every polarized analytic variation on a punctured disk.
strategy: Assume AC. Induct on the rank of a nonzero pure geometric object H, using the complex socle W_C = socle of the monodromy module ([[def-socle-of-a-module]]). (1) By [[lem-regular-trace-kernel-descends-the-complex-socle]] W_C=W_Q tensor C for a nonzero rational flat subspace; intersecting W_Q with the full integral lattice of H and clearing denominators gives a monodromy-stable integral lattice, so monodromy acts on det W_C by +-1 and its square is a constant subsystem of a geometric tensor object. (2) For a complex simple flat T <= W_C choose a flat complement T' by semisimplicity of W_C; the squared determinant line det(W)^{otimes 2} is fixed, so the Hodge torus carries det T and det T' to flat lines in geometric tensor objects by the fixed-part theorem [[thm-fixed-part-for-geometric-polarizable-variations-on-smooth-algebraic-bases]], and the Plucker description recovers that tT is a flat subspace. (3) Irreducibility is open among flat d-planes: a limit of reducible flat d-planes would produce, via compactness of the complex Grassmannian Gr(d,H_C) ([[def-stiefel-space-grassmannian-and-tautological-bundle]], [[cor-heine-borel-in-the-product-topology]], [[thm-continuous-image-of-a-compact-space-is-compact]]), a flat proper nonzero subplane of the limit, a contradiction; hence tT is simple for t near 1 and lies in the socle, so tW=W for t in a neighbourhood of the identity, and connectedness of the Hodge torus makes W a Hodge substructure. statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of complex projective varieties, with $X$ smooth of pure complex dimension $n$, and let $\eta$ be the first Chern class of an ample line bundle on $X$. For $K=Rf_*\mathbb Q_X[n]$, the maps $\eta^i:{}^pH^{-i}K\to{}^pH^iK$ are isomorphisms for all $i\ge0$, and $K\cong\bigoplus_i{}^pH^iK[-i]$ is a finite perverse splitting. Every ${}^pH^iK$ is a finite direct sum of intersection complexes of simple rational local systems on smooth dense opens of irreducible supports. The complexifications of those local systems are semisimple. This compact-source theorem will be used on explicit quiver-incidence projective compactifications; it does not assert a general nonprojective-source reduction.

Step 1.1. It suffices to treat each connected component of $X$ (finitely many open-closed smooth components, preserved by [F3]); such a component is irreducible. Replace $Y$ by the projective image with reduced structure, to be extended by closed-support. If the image dimension is zero, [F2] proves the whole package. Apply the induction step [F1] to obtain the package for $f$; lexicographic order on nonnegative integer pairs is well-founded, so with the zero-image base this proves it for all maps. statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Then $Rf_*k_X[n]$ is a finite direct sum of shifts of simple perverse sheaves on $Y$; equivalently all its perverse cohomology objects are semisimple and it splits into their shifted sum. This holds without any assumption that $k$ embeds in $\mathbb C$.

statement: Take $F=\mathbb C$, $\xi=-1$ (so $e=2$), level one $\Lambda_0$ and $d=2$. Then $H^\Lambda_2=H_{\mathbb C,-1}(S_2)$ with $T_1^2=-2T_1-1$, i.e. $(T_1+1)^2=0$; the algebra is $\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$ with $t=T_1+1$, a local algebra whose unique simple is $D=\mathbb C$ with $t$ acting as $0$, and whose regular module is the unique indecomposable projective $P=H^\Lambda_2$. Both partitions of $2$ have content $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ in the charge-$0$ convention, so $\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ is the only nonzero block and $H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}=\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$; its transported grading has $\deg t=2$ (the KLR block is the rank-two $e=2$ block $F[t]/(t^2)$ with $\deg y_2=2$). The graded Specht modules are the one-dimensional modules $S(2)=\mathbb C$ and $S(1,1)=\mathbb C$, both with trivial underlying action of $t$, and the graded composition series of $P$ is $0\subset tP\subset P$ with $tP\cong D\{2\}$, so $$[P]=(1+q^2)[D]\quad\text{in }G_0^{\rm gr}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1}),\qquad [P]\notin\{[D],q^{\pm1}[D],\dots\}.$$ The restricted label is $(1,1)$ (since $(1,1)$ is $2$-restricted and $(2)$ is not), the edge degrees of the two shapes are $\deg(S(1,1))=0$ and $\deg(S(2))=1$, so the graded Specht classes are $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ and $[S(2)]=q[D]$, and the level-one Fock data give $G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}$ and $G^*(1,1)=(M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)})/(1+q^2)$; hence under the transported identifications of [[thm-ariki-canonical-basis-theorem-in-characteristic-zero]] $$[P]\longmapsto G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}=(1+q^2)G^*(1,1),\qquad [D]\longmapsto G^*(1,1).$$ The graded Cartan pairing of [[def-graded-cartan-pairing-between-projectives-and-modules]] has $h([P],[D])=1$ and $h([P],[P])=1+q^2$, while the graded composition multiplicity is $[P:D]_q=1+q^2$ (ungraded value $2$). Thus the projective class $[P]$ is not a simple class, and the two bases are dual to each other under $h$ without being equal as classes. All computations are finite and explicit; choice is inherited only through the transported identifications cited.
